key_findings_en: A retrospective single-center study found that adults aged 80 years and older with hMPV pneumonia had higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features compared to younger adults. [news-de35c672a1f12c7c]

A computational study designed two mRNA vaccine candidates targeting the glycoprotein of human metapneumovirus (HMPV). The results are based on immunoinformatic predictions and await experimental confirmation. [news-1d86c72887a12e10]

The family experienced a series of fevers and infections caused by human metapneumovirus (hMPV) among three children, with the eldest son (Gin) initially infected and the second son (Kan) later developing symptoms. papers.title: Human Metapneumovirus Diagnosis, Pathogenesis, and Therapeutics
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a globally prevalent respiratory pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections across all age groups, with the greatest disease burden in young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Clinical manifestations range from mild upper respiratory tract symptoms, including cough, wheezing, and sore throat, to severe lower respiratory tract disease such as bronchiolitis, pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and secondary bacterial infections that may require intensive care and mechanical ventilation. Despite its widespread circulation and substantial healthcare impact, important aspects of hMPV transmission, pathogenesis, and host immune responses remain incompletely understood, hindering the development of effective therapeutics and vaccines. This review summarizes the current knowledge of hMPV epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostics, pathogenesis, and prevention strategies, with emphasis on recent outbreaks that highlight its seasonal and geographic variability. We discuss the viral life cycle and the contributions of the major surface glycoproteins—fusion (F), attachment (G), and small hydrophobic (SH) proteins—to viral infectivity, immune evasion, and disease progression. Advances in molecular diagnostics, including reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), next-generation sequencing, metagenomic approaches, and nanopore sequencing, are also examined. While supportive care remains the cornerstone of clinical management, existing antiviral therapies demonstrate limited and inconsistent efficacy. Emerging preventive and therapeutic strategies, including mRNA-based vaccines and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, offer promising avenues for disease control. Improved understanding of hMPV biology and host-pathogen interactions will be critical for developing effective interventions to reduce the global burden of this increasingly recognized respiratory pathogen.

papers.title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
papers.abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

papers.abstract_zh: 引言:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可在不同年龄段人群中引发感染,尤其是在幼儿、免疫功能低下者及老年人中。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或针对人偏肺病毒的特异性治疗方法,亟需进一步研究治疗和预防策略。方法:通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。结果:研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,触发免疫应答,这些免疫应答既有助于病毒清除,也会导致疾病发病机制。正在研发的治疗方法,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但仍需进一步验证。免疫调节剂和中草药可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的有效性尚未得到证实。疫苗研发取得进展,多个候选疫苗已进入临床前及早期临床阶段。讨论:由于人偏肺病毒的季节性流行、与其他呼吸道病毒的临床相似性以及缺乏特异性治疗方法,该病毒继续对公共卫生构成重大负担。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度增加,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管目前主要采用支持性治疗,但新兴的抗病毒药物和疫苗可能为未来提供解决方案。改善诊断可及性、提高公众意识及开展针对性研究对于控制人偏肺病毒感染至关重要。结论:由于缺乏针对性治疗方法和疫苗,人偏肺病毒继续对公共卫生构成挑战。针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。亟需进一步临床试验以确立安全有效的治疗方案。

papers.full_text: Abstract Introduction Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a significant viral pathogen associated with acute lower respiratory tract infections, particularly in elderly people. However, data on the clinical characteristics and outcomes of hMPV pneumonia among elderly people remain sparse. Methods We retrospectively reviewed data from 106 adult patients with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV infection and radiologically confirmed pneumonia diagnosed at Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital between September 2022 and March 2025. Baseline characteristics, treatment, and clinical outcomes were analyzed by age group (< 80 vs. ≥80 years). Results The 106 patients had a median age of 71 years, and 37.8% of them were male. Hypertension (43.4%), malignancy (24.5%), and diabetes mellitus (24.5%) were the most common comorbidities. The patients were categorized into two age groups: <80 years (n = 79, 74.5%) and ≥ 80 years (n = 27, 25.5%). Patients aged ≥ 80 years had a significantly higher prevalence of hypertension (63.0% vs. 36.7%, p = 0.017), dementia (22.2% vs. 5.1%, p = 0.016), multilobar involvement (92.6% vs. 74.7%, p = 0.048), and pleural effusion (22.2% vs. 3.8%, p = 0.008). Additional microorganisms were detected in 32.1% of patients, with bacterial organisms alone (24.5%) being more common than viral organisms alone (5.7%); Haemophilus influenzae and Klebsiella pneumoniae were the most frequently detected bacteria. The overall hospitalization rate was 82.1% and was significantly higher among patients aged ≥ 80 years (96.3% vs. 77.2%, p = 0.038). ICU admission rates were numerically higher in patients aged ≥ 80 years (25.9% vs. 10.1%), although the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.150). In multivariable analysis among hospitalized patients, greater initial oxygen requirement was associated with longer hospitalization. Conclusion Adults aged ≥ 80 years with hMPV pneumonia had higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features in age-group comparisons. These findings highlight the substantial clinical burden of hMPV pneumonia in older adults and the importance of careful assessment of disease severity at presentation. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the clinical characteristics and outcomes of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) pneumonia in elderly patients, as data on this specific population remain limited. A retrospective analysis of 106 adult patients with hMPV infection and pneumonia diagnosed between September 2022 and March 2025 revealed that those aged ≥80 years had higher rates of comorbidities, more severe radiologic features, and greater hospitalization rates compared to younger patients. The study highlights the substantial clinical burden of hMPV pneumonia in older adults and underscores the importance of careful disease severity assessment. While the study is limited by its retrospective nature, the use of polymerase chain reaction and radiological confirmation strengthens the evidence, leading to a moderate confidence assessment.

papers.title: Co-Assembly of Ribavirin and TMC353121 Nanoparticles for Enhanced Inhibition of Respiratory Syncytial Virus-Induced Pneumonia as an Alternative Therapy

source_records.title: Co-Assembly of Ribavirin and TMC353121 Nanoparticles for Enhanced Inhibition of Respiratory Syncytial Virus-Induced Pneumonia as an Alternative Therapy

papers.priority_tier_reason: 高相关性，且具备高等级研究设计、全文证据或较强数据库/引用支持
papers.full_text: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of acute respiratory infection requiring hospitalization in children worldwide. Although no combination therapies exist for RSV, ribavirin (RBA) and TMC353121 (TMC) can efficiently combat RSV through different mechanisms. We investigated the feasibility of formulating RBA and TMC into an RBA-TMC self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) and assessed its antiviral activity. Our results showed that RBA and TMC formed RTSN through hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions. Cellular studies indicated that RTSN exhibited remarkable antioxidant, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory properties. RTSN showed antiviral efficacy, with a selectivity index of 43.8 and an effective concentration (EC50) of 10.9 μM. Moreover, RTSN was used to treat a mouse model of the respiratory syncytial virus-induced pneumonia (RSVIP) via multiple mechanisms, including mitigating oxidative stress, reducing viral load, and modulating macrophage polarization, while maintaining promising biosafety. Overall, this study presents an innovative treatment strategy for RSV and highlights the benefits of self-assembly technology in augmenting potential. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of acute respiratory infection requiring hospitalization in children worldwide. Although no combination therapies exist for RSV, ribavirin (RBA) and TMC353121 (TMC) can efficiently combat RSV through different mechanisms. We investigated the feasibility of formulating RBA and TMC into an RBA-TMC self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) and assessed its antiviral activity. Our results showed that RBA and TMC formed RTSN through hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions. Cellular studies indicated that RTSN exhibited remarkable antioxidant, antiviral, and anti-inflammatory properties. RTSN showed antiviral efficacy, with a selectivity index of 43.8 and an effective concentration (EC50) of 10.9 μM. Moreover, RTSN was used to treat a mouse model of the respiratory syncytial virus-induced pneumonia (RSVIP) via multiple mechanisms, including mitigating oxidative stress, reducing viral load, and modulating macrophage polarization, while maintaining promising biosafety. Overall, this study presents an innovative treatment strategy for RSV and highlights the benefits of self-assembly technology in augmenting potential. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the feasibility of formulating ribavirin and TMC353121 into a self-assembled nanoparticle (RTSN) to enhance antiviral activity against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-induced pneumonia. The research demonstrates that RTSN can effectively combat RSV through multiple mechanisms, including reducing viral load and modulating macrophage polarization. The findings suggest that RTSN could serve as an innovative treatment strategy for RSV, highlighting the potential of self-assembly technology in antiviral applications. However, the study is limited to experimental models, and the evidence is moderate due to the absence of human clinical trials. The results may inform future research into alternative therapies for RSV and contribute to the development of more effective antiviral treatments.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过研究将核苷类药物和TMC353121制成自组装纳米颗粒(RTSN)的可行性,探索RSV诱导肺炎的替代疗法,并增强抗病毒药物活性。呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是全球范围内导致儿童需要住院的急性呼吸道感染的主要原因。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用了呼吸道合胞病毒诱导肺炎(RSVIP)的小鼠模型进行体外和体内实验。研究通过多种机制(包括减轻氧化应激、降低病毒载量和调节巨噬细胞极化)评估了RTSN的抗病毒药物活性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过氢键和π-π堆积作用将核苷类药物和TMC353121制成RTSN。进行了细胞研究以评估RTSN的抗氧化、抗病毒药物和抗炎特性,并在RSV诱导肺炎的小鼠模型中测试了其疗效。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示,RTSN表现出抗病毒药物的显著疗效,其选择性指数为43.8,有效浓度(EC50)为10.9 μM。此外,还发现RTSN具有有希望的生物安全性特征。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为证明RTSN作为RSV创新治疗策略的潜力。本研究突出了自组装技术在增强抗病毒药物活性方面的优势。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RTSN可能为RSV诱导肺炎提供一种新的治疗途径,从而可能改善治疗选择并减少儿童因RSV相关住院而带来的负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外和体内实验,可能无法完全代表临床结果。由于结果基于实验模型而非人体试验,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过研究将核苷类药物和TMC353121制成自组装纳米颗粒(RTSN)的可行性,探索RSV诱导肺炎的替代疗法,并增强抗病毒药物活性。呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是全球范围内导致儿童需要住院的急性呼吸道感染的主要原因。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用了呼吸道合胞病毒诱导肺炎(RSVIP)的小鼠模型进行体外和体内实验。研究通过多种机制(包括减轻氧化应激、降低病毒载量和调节巨噬细胞极化)评估了RTSN的抗病毒药物活性。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员通过氢键和π-π堆积作用将核苷类药物和TMC353121制成RTSN。进行了细胞研究以评估RTSN的抗氧化、抗病毒药物和抗炎特性,并在RSV诱导肺炎的小鼠模型中测试了其疗效。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果显示,RTSN表现出抗病毒药物的显著疗效,其选择性指数为43.8,有效浓度(EC50)为10.9 μM。此外,还发现RTSN具有有希望的生物安全性特征。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为证明RTSN作为RSV创新治疗策略的潜力。本研究突出了自组装技术在增强抗病毒药物活性方面的优势。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RTSN可能为RSV诱导肺炎提供一种新的治疗途径,从而可能改善治疗选择并减少儿童因RSV相关住院而带来的负担。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外和体内实验,可能无法完全代表临床结果。由于结果基于实验模型而非人体试验,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Viral etiology and predictors of hospitalization in adults younger than 65 years with laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral infections in the pre-COVID era
papers.abstract: Respiratory viral tract infections (VRTIs) are generally considered more severe in older adults, while their clinical impact in younger adults remains less well characterized. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of adults aged 18–64 years with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), or parainfluenza virus (PIV) infection during the 2016–2018 respiratory seasons. Among 172 patients, 110 had influenza, 31 RSV, 17 hMPV, and 14 PIV infections. Hospitalization occurred in 64.0% of patients overall, with rates of 53.6% for influenza, 77.4% for RSV, and 87.1% for hMPV/PIV infections. Chronic respiratory disease, neutrophilia, and hMPV/PIV infection were independently associated with hospitalization. Chronic respiratory disease and previous respiratory tract infection were independently associated with lower odds of short-term favorable outcome, whereas detectable eosinophils were associated with improved recovery. Ninety-day mortality was low across viral groups. Age was not independently associated with hospitalization or short-term recovery within this restricted age range. These findings highlight substantial morbidity associated with VRTIs in adults younger than 65 years and underscore the need for greater attention to this population, which remains less well characterized than older adults.

papers.title: In silico conservation and HLA-binding profiles of HMPV F and G protein epitopes: implications for universal vaccine development.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a significant cause of respiratory infection, yet no licensed vaccine exists. Variability across viral subgroups, particularly in the attachment (G) protein, can complicate universal design. We assessed the immunogenetic regions in the fusion (F) and G proteins to identify stable vaccine targets. METHODS: We analyzed N = 324 Pittsburgh and N = 655 global HMPV genomes (2017-2022) for genome diversity per viral subgroup. Previously identified epitope sequences were obtained from the Immune Epitope DataBase (IEDB) for F and G proteins and sequence similarity was determined. Using NetMHCpan-4.1, we identified and computed inferred human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding affinities for 15 epitope variants (1 or 2 substitutions) against universally common human alleles. RESULTS: The F protein was highly conserved across all subgroups (>96% amino acid sequence identity). In the G protein, we identified a conserved epitope cluster (G3-G7) where epitope G7 was present in 91% of A2 genomes. Functional modeling of the G-protein epitope variants revealed that the majority of HLA alleles maintained or gained binding affinity, a subset exhibited diminished binding (escape), suggesting these regions are subject to ongoing antigenic drift. B-genotypes showed fewer retained binders and were notably underrepresented in the current epitope databases. CONCLUSION: The conserved F protein remains an optimal target for neutralization, while the G3-G7 cluster provides a robust secondary target for T-cell mediated immunity. A bivalent vaccine strategy could pair the stable F protein with these high-frequency G-protein epitopes to elicit an immune response. This approach addresses the A2 subgroup, and incorporating B-genotypes through ongoing surveillance and epitope mapping will be essential to achieve comprehensive, multi-antigen coverage across circulating HMPV strains.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify stable vaccine targets in the fusion (F) and G proteins of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) to address the lack of a licensed vaccine and the variability across viral subgroups, particularly in the G protein.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed N = 324 Pittsburgh and N = 655 global HMPV genomes (2017-2022) to assess the immunogenetic regions in the F and G proteins.
analysis.methods: The researchers used N = 324 Pittsburgh and N = 655 global HMPV genomes (2017-2022) for genome diversity analysis and obtained previously identified epitope sequences from the Immune Epitope DataBase (IEDB) for F and G proteins, then used NetMHCpan-4.1 to compute inferred human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding affinities for 15 epitope variants (1 or 2 substitutions) against universally common human alleles.
analysis.main_results: The F protein was highly conserved across all subgroups (>96% amino acid sequence identity), and a conserved epitope cluster (G3-G7) was identified in the G protein, with epitope G7 present in 91% of A2 genomes. Functional modeling revealed that the majority of HLA alleles maintained or gained binding affinity, while a subset exhibited diminished binding (escape).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified the conserved F protein as an optimal target for neutralization and the G3-G7 cluster as a robust secondary target for T-cell mediated immunity, suggesting a bivalent vaccine strategy could be effective.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a bivalent vaccine strategy pairing the stable F protein with high-frequency G-protein epitopes could address the A2 subgroup and incorporate B-genotypes through ongoing surveillance and epitope mapping to achieve comprehensive, multi-antigen coverage across circulating HMPV strains.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on in silico analysis and the potential for ongoing antigenic drift in the G protein, which may affect the stability of the identified epitopes. The evidence strength is moderate due to the in silico nature of the analysis.

analysis.summary_en: The study identified the conserved F protein and the G3-G7 cluster in the G protein as stable targets for a bivalent vaccine strategy against human metapneumovirus (HMPV), addressing the lack of a licensed vaccine and variability in viral subgroups.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在识别人偏肺病毒(HMPV)F和G蛋白中的稳定疫苗靶点,以应对缺乏获批的疫苗以及病毒亚群间的变异性,尤其是在G蛋白中。

elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用了N = 324匹兹堡和N = 655全球HMPV 基因组(2017-2022)进行基因组多样性分析,并从免疫表位数据库(IEDB)获取了之前鉴定的F和G蛋白表位序列,随后利用NetMHCpan-4.1计算了15个表位变体(1或2个取代)对普遍人类等位基因的推断人类白细胞抗原(HLA)结合亲和力。
elements_zh.main_results: F蛋白在所有亚群中高度保守(>96%的氨基酸序列同源性),并且在G蛋白中鉴定出一个保守的表位簇(G3-G7),其中表位G7在91%的A2亚群基因组中存在。功能建模显示,大多数HLA等位基因保持或增强了结合亲和力,而部分等位基因表现出结合亲和力下降(逃逸)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究确定了保守的F蛋白作为中和的最优靶点,并将G3-G7簇作为T细胞介导免疫的稳健次级靶点,表明一种双价疫苗策略可能是有效的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,一种将稳定F蛋白与高频率G蛋白表位配对的双价疫苗策略可能能够应对A2亚群,并通过持续的监测和表位映射纳入B型基因组,从而实现对流行HMPV株的全面、多抗原覆盖。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于依赖于体外分析,且由于G蛋白可能持续发生抗原漂变,所鉴定的表位稳定性可能受到影响。由于分析的体外性质,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 人偏肺病毒(HMPV)F和G蛋白表位的体外保守性和HLA结合特征:对开发通用疫苗的启示。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a significant cause of respiratory infection, yet no licensed vaccine exists. Variability across viral subgroups, particularly in the attachment (G) protein, can complicate universal design. We assessed the immunogenetic regions in the fusion (F) and G proteins to identify stable vaccine targets. METHODS: We analyzed N = 324 Pittsburgh and N = 655 global HMPV genomes (2017-2022) for genome diversity per viral subgroup. Previously identified epitope sequences were obtained from the Immune Epitope DataBase (IEDB) for F and G proteins and sequence similarity was determined. Using NetMHCpan-4.1, we identified and computed inferred human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding affinities for 15 epitope variants (1 or 2 substitutions) against universally common human alleles. RESULTS: The F protein was highly conserved across all subgroups (>96% amino acid sequence identity). In the G protein, we identified a conserved epitope cluster (G3-G7) where epitope G7 was present in 91% of A2 genomes. Functional modeling of the G-protein epitope variants revealed that the majority of HLA alleles maintained or gained binding affinity, a subset exhibited diminished binding (escape), suggesting these regions are subject to ongoing antigenic drift. B-genotypes showed fewer retained binders and were notably underrepresented in the current epitope databases. CONCLUSION: The conserved F protein remains an optimal target for neutralization, while the G3-G7 cluster provides a robust secondary target for T-cell mediated immunity. A bivalent vaccine strategy could pair the stable F protein with these high-frequency G-protein epitopes to elicit an immune response. This approach addresses the A2 subgroup, and incorporating B-genotypes through ongoing surveillance and epitope mapping will be essential to achieve comprehensive, multi-antigen coverage across circulating HMPV strains.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是呼吸道感染的重要病原体,但目前尚无获批的疫苗。病毒亚群间的变异性,尤其是在附着(G)蛋白中,可能阻碍通用疫苗的设计。我们评估了F和G蛋白中的免疫遗传区域,以确定稳定的疫苗靶点。方法:我们分析了N = 324匹兹堡和N = 655全球HMPV 基因组(2017-2022),以评估各病毒亚群的基因组多样性。从免疫表位数据库(IEDB)获取了之前鉴定的F和G蛋白表位序列,并确定了序列相似性。利用NetMHCpan-4.1,我们鉴定了并计算了15个表位变体(1或2个取代)对普遍人类等位基因的推断人类白细胞抗原(HLA)结合亲和力。结果:F蛋白在所有亚群中高度保守(>96%的氨基酸序列同源性)。在G蛋白中,我们鉴定出一个保守的表位簇(G3-G7),其中表位G7在91%的A2亚群基因组中存在。G蛋白表位变体的功能建模显示,大多数HLA等位基因保持或增强了结合亲和力,而部分等位基因表现出结合亲和力下降(逃逸),这表明这些区域可能正在经历持续的抗原漂变。B型基因组显示出较少的保留结合位点,并且在当前的表位数据库中显著代表性不足。结论:高度保守的F蛋白仍然是中和的最优靶点,而G3-G7簇则为T细胞介导的免疫提供了稳健的次级靶点。一种双价疫苗策略可以将稳定的F蛋白与这些高频率的G蛋白表位结合,以引发有效的免疫应答。这种方法可以应对A2亚群,并通过持续的监测和表位映射纳入B型基因组,从而实现对流行HMPV株的全面、多抗原覆盖。

papers.title: Detection profiles and co-detection patterns of respiratory pathogens in hospitalized patients with acute respiratory infections after the COVID-19 pandemic in Nantong, China
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory-pathogen circulation may have changed after relaxation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) control measures. We characterized the pathogen spectrum, clinical-site distribution, age-specific patterns, co-detection patterns, and seasonality among hospitalized patients with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) in Nantong, China. Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study included 5,808 patients hospitalized with ARTIs at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University between December 2023 and December 2025. Respiratory specimens collected at admission were tested for 16 pathogens using multiplex real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Pathogen detection was compared by infection site, age group, and season. False discovery rate correction, multivariable logistic regression, and Cochran-Armitage trend tests were applied as appropriate. Results At least one pathogen was detected in 3,129 of 5,808 patients (53.87%). Single and mixed detections occurred in 2,103 (36.21%) and 1,026 (17.67%) patients, respectively. Klebsiella pneumoniae , Staphylococcus aureus , and Haemophilus influenzae were the most frequently detected bacterial targets. After false discovery rate correction, Mycoplasma pneumoniae , adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, H. influenzae , parainfluenza virus type III, and influenza B virus were more frequently detected in lower than upper respiratory tract infections (all q < 0.05). In adjusted analyses, M. influenzae remained associated with lower respiratory tract infections. pneumoniae detection peaked among children aged 6–17 years (30.92%, 81/262; P-trend < 0.001). Among patients with mixed detections, bacterial-bacterial pairs were most frequent, particularly S. Influenza A virus showed a marked winter peak (21.31% vs. 1.20–2.54% in other seasons; q < 0.001). Conclusion Hospitalized patients in eastern China showed frequent bacterial-target detection, age-related heterogeneity, and distinct seasonal patterns. The school-age peak in M. pneumoniae and the winter peak in influenza A virus support age- and season-informed surveillance. Because molecular detection cannot distinguish active infection from colonization, bacterial findings should be interpreted alongside clinical, culture, and biomarker data.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate changes in respiratory-pathogen circulation, including human metapneumovirus, after the relaxation of COVID-19 control measures. The background suggests that such changes may have occurred, necessitating updated surveillance strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 5,808 patients hospitalized with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) at the Affiliated Hospital of Nantong University in China between December 2023 and December 2025. The study characterized the pathogen spectrum, clinical-site distribution, age-specific patterns, co-detection patterns, and seasonality among these patients.
analysis.methods: Respiratory specimens collected at admission were tested for 16 pathogens, including human metapneumovirus, using multiplex real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. False discovery rate correction, multivariable logistic regression, and Cochran-Armitage trend tests were applied as appropriate to analyze the data.
analysis.main_results: At least one pathogen was detected in 3,129 of 5,808 patients (53.87%). Single and mixed detections occurred in 2,103 (36.21%) and 1,026 (17.67%) patients, respectively. Human metapneumovirus detection peaked among children aged 6–17 years (30.92%, 81/262; P-trend < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the distinct seasonal patterns of human metapneumovirus, with a marked winter peak in influenza A virus and a school-age peak in human metapneumovirus. These findings support the need for age- and season-informed surveillance strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and prevention strategies for human metapneumovirus, particularly in children and during specific seasons. They also emphasize the importance of integrating clinical, culture, and biomarker data for accurate interpretation of molecular detection results.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on molecular detection, which cannot distinguish active infection from colonization. Despite these limitations, the evidence is moderate due to the use of statistical corrections and trend tests.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated changes in respiratory-pathogen circulation, including human metapneumovirus, in hospitalized patients with acute respiratory infections in Nantong, China, after the relaxation of COVID-19 control measures. A retrospective cross-sectional design was used, analyzing 5,808 patients admitted between December 2023 and December 2025. Respiratory specimens were tested for 16 pathogens, including human metapneumovirus, using multiplex real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. The results showed that at least one pathogen was detected in 53.87% of patients, with human metapneumovirus detection peaking among children aged 6–17 years. The study highlights the distinct seasonal patterns of human metapneumovirus and supports the need for age- and season-informed surveillance. However, the study's reliance on molecular detection, which cannot distinguish active infection from colonization, limits its conclusions. The evidence is moderate due to the use of statistical corrections and trend tests.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性横断面研究纳入了2023年12月至2025年12月期间在南通大学附属医院住院的5,808名急性呼吸道感染(ARTIs)患者。研究分析了这些患者中的病原体谱系、临床部位分布、年龄特异性模式、共检模式及季节性。
elements_zh.methods: 在入院时收集的呼吸道标本通过多重实时定量聚合酶链反应检测了16种病原体,包括人偏肺病毒。根据需要应用了错误发现率校正、多变量逻辑回归和Cochran-Armitage趋势检验来分析数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 在5,808名患者中,至少检测到一种病原体的有3,129名(53.87%)。单检和混合检分别发生在2,103名(36.21%)和1,026名(17.67%)患者中。人偏肺病毒检测在6-17岁儿童中达到峰值(30.92%,81/262;P-trend < 0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究突出了人偏肺病毒的季节性模式,其中流感A病毒在冬季达到显著高峰,而人偏肺病毒在学龄儿童中达到高峰。这些发现支持基于年龄和季节的监测策略的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为针对人偏肺病毒的监测和预防策略提供依据,特别是在儿童群体和特定季节。它们还强调了将临床、培养和生物标志物数据整合起来以准确解读分子检测结果的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计和依赖分子检测,而分子检测无法区分活跃感染与定植。尽管存在这些局限性,由于使用了统计校正和趋势检验,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 在放松新冠病毒疾病2019(COVID-19)防控措施后,呼吸道病原体的流行可能发生了变化。我们分析了江苏省南通市住院急性呼吸道感染(ARTIs)患者中的病原体谱系、临床部位分布、年龄特异性模式、共检模式及季节性。方法 本回顾性横断面研究纳入了2023年12月至2025年12月期间在南通大学附属医院住院的5,808名急性呼吸道感染患者。在入院时收集的呼吸道标本通过多重实时定量聚合酶链反应检测了16种病原体。根据感染部位、年龄组和季节比较病原体检测结果。根据需要应用了错误发现率校正、多变量逻辑回归和Cochran-Armitage趋势检验。结果 在5,808名患者中,至少检测到一种病原体的有3,129名(53.87%)。单检和混合检分别发生在2,103名(36.21%)和1,026名(17.67%)患者中。克雷伯氏肺炎杆菌、金黄色葡萄球菌和流感嗜血杆菌是最常检测到的细菌靶标。在错误发现率校正后,肺炎支原体、腺病毒、人偏肺病毒、流感嗜血杆菌、副流感病毒III型和流感B病毒在下呼吸道感染中比上呼吸道感染更常见(所有q < 0.05)。在调整分析中,肺炎支原体仍与下呼吸道感染检测相关。肺炎支原体检测在6-17岁儿童中达到峰值(30.92%,81/262;P-trend < 0.001)。在混合检测患者中,细菌-细菌对最常见,特别是S. 腺病毒在冬季达到显著高峰(21.31% vs. 其他季节的1.20-2.54%;q < 0.001)。结论 江苏省南通市住院患者中表现出频繁的细菌靶标检测、年龄相关的异质性和独特的季节性模式。肺炎支原体的学龄儿童高峰和流感A病毒的冬季高峰支持基于年龄和季节的监测策略。由于分子检测无法区分活跃感染与定植,细菌检测结果应结合临床、培养和生物标志物数据进行解读。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性横断面研究纳入了2023年12月至2025年12月期间在南通大学附属医院住院的5,808名急性呼吸道感染(ARTIs)患者。研究分析了这些患者中的病原体谱系、临床部位分布、年龄特异性模式、共检模式及季节性。
analysis_zh.methods: 在入院时收集的呼吸道标本通过多重实时定量聚合酶链反应检测了16种病原体,包括人偏肺病毒。根据需要应用了错误发现率校正、多变量逻辑回归和Cochran-Armitage趋势检验来分析数据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在5,808名患者中,至少检测到一种病原体的有3,129名(53.87%)。单检和混合检分别发生在2,103名(36.21%)和1,026名(17.67%)患者中。人偏肺病毒检测在6-17岁儿童中达到峰值(30.92%,81/262;P-trend < 0.001)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究突出了人偏肺病毒的季节性模式,其中流感A病毒在冬季达到显著高峰,而人偏肺病毒在学龄儿童中达到高峰。这些发现支持基于年龄和季节的监测策略的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为针对人偏肺病毒的监测和预防策略提供依据,特别是在儿童群体和特定季节。它们还强调了将临床、培养和生物标志物数据整合起来以准确解读分子检测结果的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计和依赖分子检测,而分子检测无法区分活跃感染与定植。尽管存在这些局限性,由于使用了统计校正和趋势检验,证据强度中等。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, October 29, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Human metapneumovirus pneumonia hits hardest in adults aged 80 and over by October 27, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Human metapneumovirus pneumonia hits hardest in adults aged 80 and over Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Adults aged 80 years and older who develop pneumonia from human metapneumovirus face substantially higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features than younger adults, according to a retrospective single-center study of 106 patients published in BMC Infectious Diseases. Human metapneumovirus is a significant viral pathogen associated with acute lower respiratory tract infections, particularly in elderly people, yet data on the clinical characteristics and outcomes of hMPV pneumonia among elderly people remain sparse. The researchers, led by Hyeon Hwa Kim and Yon Ju Ryu of Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital, reviewed records from 106 adult patients with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV infection and radiologically confirmed pneumonia diagnosed at their hospital between September 2022 and March 2025. The cohort had a median age of 71 years, and 37.8% of the patients were male. Hypertension was the most common comorbidity, present in 43.4% of patients, followed by malignancy and diabetes mellitus, each affecting 24.5%. To examine how age shaped the disease course, the patients were divided into two groups: those younger than 80 years, who numbered 79 and made up 74.5% of the cohort, and those aged 80 years or older, who numbered 27 and made up 25.5%. The age-group comparisons revealed several significant differences. Patients aged 80 and older had a higher prevalence of hypertension, at 63.0% versus 36.7% in the younger group, and of dementia, at 22.2% versus 5.1%. Their chest imaging also showed more extensive disease, with multilobar involvement in 92.6% versus 74.7% and pleural effusion in 22.2% versus 3.8%. These differences in hypertension, dementia, multilobar involvement, and pleural effusion were all statistically significant. Co-infection was a notable feature of the cohort. Additional microorganisms were detected in 32.1% of patients, and bacterial organisms alone were more common than viral organisms alone, at 24.5% versus 5.7%. Haemophilus influenzae and Klebsiella pneumoniae were the most frequently detected bacteria among the co-pathogens. The overall hospitalization rate was 82.1%, and it was significantly higher among patients aged 80 and older, at 96.3% versus 77.2% in the younger group. Intensive care unit admission rates were numerically higher in the older group, at 25.9% versus 10.1%, although this difference did not reach statistical significance. Within the hospitalized subgroup, the researchers performed a multivariable analysis to identify factors linked to length of stay. Greater initial oxygen requirement was associated with longer hospitalization, indicating that the degree of respiratory support needed at presentation tracked with how long patients remained in hospital. The authors conclude that adults aged 80 years and older with hMPV pneumonia had higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features in the age-group comparisons, and they highlight the substantial clinical burden of hMPV pneumonia in older adults and the importance of careful assessment of disease severity at presentation. As a retrospective analysis of patients at a single hospital, the study describes associations observed in one cohort rather than causal effects, and the ICU admission finding did not reach statistical significance. The findings nonetheless add to the limited evidence base on hMPV pneumonia in the very old, a group in which the virus appears to impose a heavier clinical burden. news.content_original: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, October 29, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Human metapneumovirus pneumonia hits hardest in adults aged 80 and over by October 27, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Human metapneumovirus pneumonia hits hardest in adults aged 80 and over Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Adults aged 80 years and older who develop pneumonia from human metapneumovirus face substantially higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features than younger adults, according to a retrospective single-center study of 106 patients published in BMC Infectious Diseases. Human metapneumovirus is a significant viral pathogen associated with acute lower respiratory tract infections, particularly in elderly people, yet data on the clinical characteristics and outcomes of hMPV pneumonia among elderly people remain sparse. The researchers, led by Hyeon Hwa Kim and Yon Ju Ryu of Ewha Womans University Seoul Hospital, reviewed records from 106 adult patients with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV infection and radiologically confirmed pneumonia diagnosed at their hospital between September 2022 and March 2025. The cohort had a median age of 71 years, and 37.8% of the patients were male. Hypertension was the most common comorbidity, present in 43.4% of patients, followed by malignancy and diabetes mellitus, each affecting 24.5%. To examine how age shaped the disease course, the patients were divided into two groups: those younger than 80 years, who numbered 79 and made up 74.5% of the cohort, and those aged 80 years or older, who numbered 27 and made up 25.5%. The age-group comparisons revealed several significant differences. Patients aged 80 and older had a higher prevalence of hypertension, at 63.0% versus 36.7% in the younger group, and of dementia, at 22.2% versus 5.1%. Their chest imaging also showed more extensive disease, with multilobar involvement in 92.6% versus 74.7% and pleural effusion in 22.2% versus 3.8%. These differences in hypertension, dementia, multilobar involvement, and pleural effusion were all statistically significant. Co-infection was a notable feature of the cohort. Additional microorganisms were detected in 32.1% of patients, and bacterial organisms alone were more common than viral organisms alone, at 24.5% versus 5.7%. Haemophilus influenzae and Klebsiella pneumoniae were the most frequently detected bacteria among the co-pathogens. The overall hospitalization rate was 82.1%, and it was significantly higher among patients aged 80 and older, at 96.3% versus 77.2% in the younger group. Intensive care unit admission rates were numerically higher in the older group, at 25.9% versus 10.1%, although this difference did not reach statistical significance. Within the hospitalized subgroup, the researchers performed a multivariable analysis to identify factors linked to length of stay. Greater initial oxygen requirement was associated with longer hospitalization, indicating that the degree of respiratory support needed at presentation tracked with how long patients remained in hospital. The authors conclude that adults aged 80 years and older with hMPV pneumonia had higher hospitalization rates and more severe clinical and radiologic features in the age-group comparisons, and they highlight the substantial clinical burden of hMPV pneumonia in older adults and the importance of careful assessment of disease severity at presentation. As a retrospective analysis of patients at a single hospital, the study describes associations observed in one cohort rather than causal effects, and the ICU admission finding did not reach statistical significance. The findings nonetheless add to the limited evidence base on hMPV pneumonia in the very old, a group in which the virus appears to impose a heavier clinical burden. news.content_zh: 一项于2026年10月27日发表在《BMC Infectious Diseases》上的研究发现,80岁以上成人若因人偏肺病毒(人偏肺病毒,hMPV)感染而出现肺炎,其住院率显著高于年轻成人,且临床和影像学特征更为严重。该研究在首尔女子大学医院进行,分析了2022年9月至2025年3月期间确诊为hMPV感染并伴有肺炎的106名患者。老年组(27名患者,占队列研究的25.5%)的住院率为96.3%,而年轻组(79名患者)为77.2%。此外,老年患者表现出更广泛的疾病影响,其中92.6%的患者出现多叶病变,而年轻患者为74.7%;22.2%的老年患者出现胸腔积液,而年轻患者为3.8%。高血压是最常见的合并症,影响了43.4%的患者,其次是恶性肿瘤和糖尿病。该研究突显了hMPV肺炎在老年群体中的显著临床负担,并强调了在初次就诊时对疾病严重程度进行细致评估的重要性。然而,该研究是一项回顾性单中心分析,仅描述了相关性而非因果关系。老年组的ICU入院率数值上更高,但未达到统计学显著性。

news.content_title: Preventing a Total Wipeout with 3 Kids and Human Metapneumovirus! The Reality of Being Tossed Around by Staggered Fevers and the 'Rebound After Thinking They Were Better'|ダイキチ
news.content: メインコンテンツへスキップ Preventing a Total Wipeout with 3 Kids and Human Metapneumovirus! The Reality of Being Tossed Around by Staggered Fevers and the 'Rebound After Thinking They Were Better' ダイキチ Oct 27, 2026 20:46 Hello, this is Daikichi, aiming for FIRE! The unpleasant season has arrived, from early autumn to winter, when children take turns getting sick. In our home, just recently, during a week in October, our eldest son (Gin, middle year of kindergarten) caught the "human metapneumovirus," and our household has been a bit of a battlefield ever since (bitter laugh). When you have three children (first grade, middle year of kindergarten, and under-school age), the most terrifying thing is the "chain of household infection." That feeling of despair when you breathe a sigh of relief, thinking, "Alright! The fever is down, everyone is healthy enough to go to school and kindergarten tomorrow!" only for the next child to develop a fever on a staggered schedule... Anyone raising children has experienced this at least once, right? Before we had children, we didn't get sick that often, but when you have small children, adults also get infected repeatedly without mercy. This time, I will deliver real, primary information as a "document of a certain week" in October, detailing how our family fought the ferocity of the human metapneumovirus and carried out our "team-based night isolation strategy"! 【Tuesday to Friday】Starting with a cough, and the terror of a confirmed "Human Metapneumovirus" diagnosis It started around a Tuesday or Wednesday in October. I thought my eldest son (Gin)'s cough was getting strangely bad, and then on Thursday night (early morning), he developed a fever all at once. It hit over 38 degrees Celsius. Of course, he stayed home from kindergarten on Friday. When we took him to the pediatrician on Friday morning, after a PCR test (the painful one where they shove a long swab up your nose), the diagnosis was "human metapneumovirus." 💡 What is human metapneumovirus? It is a very common infectious disease that is said to affect "almost 100% of children by age 5 (over 80% in early childhood)." Once infected, you gain some immunity, so even if you are re-infected after growing up, it is characterized by often being mild. In other words, as adults, my wife Aki and I, and our eldest daughter (Riko) who has likely already experienced it, shouldn't get too sick even if we catch it. The problem is our youngest, our second son (Kan, under-school age). If it spreads to our second son, who is still small and has little immunity, the risk of him having a high fever for days and developing bronchitis or pneumonia is the highest...! I felt a strong sense of crisis, thinking, "I must seriously put up a defensive wall and protect our second son at all costs!" So, the strategy our family immediately adopted was the 【Team-based Night Isolation Strategy】. 【Team-based Night Isolation Strategy】 ・Infection Prevention Team: Daikichi (Father), Eldest Daughter (Riko), Second Son (Kan) ・Nursing & Safety Team: Eldest Son (Gin), Mom (Aki) *Thoroughly isolated in a separate room! We decided to get through it by physically blocking contact between our infected eldest son and our second son, whom we wanted to protect the most, at least during the night. [Saturday] A night without sleep due to coughing. I thought, 'Let's go to the ENT,' but was I actually refused treatment!? Friday night, as expected, my eldest son couldn't sleep at all due to a terrible cough... It was truly pitiful to watch. 'I want to make him feel even a little better.' 'Instead of just the pediatrician's medicine, wouldn't he feel refreshed if he got his nose and throat suctioned at an ENT clinic?' My wife and I discussed this, and we decided I would take our eldest son to the ENT on Saturday. Since his fever had gone down by the morning, I was hopeful, thinking, 'Alright, he'll be able to sleep tonight.' However... when we arrived at the hospital and took his temperature, it was 37.6 degrees Celsius. Nurse: 'I'm sorry, since he has a fever, we cannot accept your visit today...' Darn it!!! I was actually refused treatment!! I had completely let my guard down thinking his fever had broken. In this day and age, with strict infection control and fever clinic rules, we hit a wall where we couldn't be seen if he had even the slightest fever. In the end, we had to turn back to the pediatrician we had visited the day before. 'Are we doing the PCR test again...?' The battle with my eldest son's hospital trauma In the car on the way to the pediatrician, my eldest son, Gin, was feeling down and on the verge of tears from fear. This was because he had undergone a painful PCR test where a swab was shoved up his nose during our visit the day before (Friday). He was terrified of going to the pediatrician, saying, 'Are we doing that painful thing again...? I don't want to...' Even for an impatient person like me, it was a struggle to persuade my reluctant eldest son. 💬 Notes on what to say to my eldest son 'We aren't doing the nose-tickle (PCR) today! We're just going to have them suction your nose!' 'Let's go to the pediatrician where you get a ramune candy when you're done!' I offered concrete reassurance and managed to take him. He was able to get a proper suctioning at the pediatrician, and the effect of the suctioning was truly immense! After we got home, his cough eased up significantly, and he slept soundly for the first time in a while. I'm so glad...! [Sunday to the following Monday] Peace of mind was short-lived... A 'summons' from kindergarten [Sunday (3rd day of fever)] My eldest son's fever had gone down, his energy had returned a bit, and his appetite had come back, so we were relieved. At night, we decided to sleep all together in a row for the first time in a while. [The following Monday (4th day of fever)] Just to be safe, we let our eldest son stay home from kindergarten that day to keep an eye on him. Our second son (Kan) had a slight fever of 37.1 degrees, but he was perfectly energetic, so we sent him off to kindergarten. ...And, our peace of mind was short-lived. In the early afternoon, we got a call from the kindergarten saying, 'Second son (Kan) has exceeded 38 degrees, so please come pick him up.' The infection of my second son, which I had been worried about, has finally become a reality...! When he came home, he had a fever, but he was acting completely normal and full of energy. This is another point where it's hard for a parent to decide what to do. [Next week, Tuesday to Wednesday] I took time off work, and just when I thought his temperature had returned to normal, the fever came back in the middle of the night... [Next week, Tuesday (Day 5 of fever)] My eldest son returned to kindergarten full of energy! My second son, who had a fever the day before, was naturally staying home. I took the day off from work to stay home and take care of him. When I woke up in the morning, my second son's fever was completely gone. He was incredibly energetic during the day and ate his meals well. I breathed a sigh of relief, thinking, 'Oh! It looks like my second son will have a mild case. In that case, he can go to kindergarten tomorrow (Wednesday)!' But then... [Next week, Wednesday (Day 6 of fever)] In the middle of the night, after the date had changed, my second son's body suddenly felt hot. When I checked his temperature, he had a fever again. Of course, it was decided that he would stay home from kindergarten on Wednesday as well. Going down, then going back up in the middle of the night... this infinite loop of 'up and down.' You really can't let your guard down until the very end when nursing someone with an infectious disease. But he's been full of energy all day long (bitter laugh). [Next week, Thursday (Day 7 of fever)] Both of them recovered safely and were able to go to kindergarten full of energy! There is still a little bit of a cough left, but for now, I'm relieved. Summary: Real, Honest Thoughts on Surviving a Never-Ending Life of Nursing Here is what I learned from this chaotic drama. [Lesson Memo from This Experience] 1. Be prepared for the time lag between 'the fever has gone down' and 'they can go to school' Even if children are energetic during the day, it is common for their fever to suddenly return in the middle of the night. It is mentally easier for parents to have a schedule of 'watching them for a full day after their temperature returns to normal.' 2. Treat paid leave and cooperation between spouses as a 'long-distance run' and divide the tasks If one person takes on all the nursing, both their work and their mental state will break down. I took paid leave to handle this, but it is essential to have a system where you can take turns taking time off. 3. Offer 'concrete reassurance' to children who are traumatized by the hospital Saying things like, 'There won't be any painful tests (PCR) today' or 'You can have a candy when we're done' was very helpful for my child who hates going to the doctor. It is truly difficult to prevent household infections while keeping up with work and daily life, but to all the fathers and mothers out there, let's keep operating in energy-saving mode and get through today as well! Believing in the day when we can laugh and say, 'That was a tough time'... #子育て #健康 #育児 #ライフスタイル #病院 #元気 #幼稚園 #長男 #次男 #感染症 #3人育児 #小児科 #お父さん #家庭内感染 #男の子パパ #子育て #健康 #育児 #ライフスタイル #病院 #元気 #幼稚園 #長男 #次男 #感染症 #3人育児 #小児科 #お父さん #家庭内感染 #男の子パパ トップ 育児・教育 子育て あなたへのおすすめ

elements_en.scale_impact_and_risk: Three children were affected, with the second son developing a fever after the eldest son. No deaths or severe complications were reported. The risk of further spread was high due to the staggered fever pattern.

news.content_title: Computational Design Yields Two mRNA Vaccine Candidates Against HMPV
news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, October 29, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Computational Design Yields Two mRNA Vaccine Candidates Against HMPV Glycoprotein by October 28, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 Computational Design Yields Two mRNA Vaccine Candidates Against HMPV Glycoprotein Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Human metapneumovirus, a leading cause of acute respiratory infections in children, older adults, and immunocompromised people, still has no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral treatment. A new computational study has taken a step toward filling that gap by designing two multi-epitope mRNA vaccine candidates against the virus’s glycoprotein, using a reverse vaccinology pipeline built entirely on immunoinformatic predictions. The work, published in Discover Immunity, reports favorable predicted antigenicity, safety, and structural properties for both constructs, while emphasizing that every result remains computational and awaits experimental confirmation. The research team, led by Elijah Kolawole Oladipo with collaborators across multiple Nigerian and international institutions, retrieved 107 human metapneumovirus glycoprotein sequences from the National Center for Biotechnology Information protein database to ensure global representation. These sequences, drawn from all available continents, were screened in two stages: first for antigenicity using VaxiJen 2.0, and then for immunogenicity using VaxiJen 3.0. Only sequences with an antigenicity score greater than 0.6 and an immunogenicity score between 66 and 100 percent advanced to epitope prediction. From the screened sequences, the researchers predicted three classes of epitopes. Cytotoxic T-lymphocyte epitopes were identified with NetCTL v1.2 and NetMHCpan 4.0, then filtered for antigenicity, toxicity, and allergenicity, yielding five final candidates. Helper T-lymphocyte epitopes were predicted through a consensus of the IEDB and NetMHCIIpan 4.0 servers, with the resulting five epitopes additionally evaluated for their capacity to induce interferon-gamma, interleukin-4, interleukin-6, and interleukin-10. Linear B-cell epitopes were predicted using ABCPred and Bepipred, producing six epitopes that passed the same safety and antigenicity filters. To reduce the risk of autoimmune cross-reactivity, all selected epitopes were subjected to BLASTp analysis against the non-redundant human proteome, with stringency thresholds including an E-value cutoff of 0.001, sequence identity below 30 percent, and query coverage under 50 percent; only epitopes showing no significant homology to human proteins were retained. The final constructs each incorporated fifteen epitopes: five B-cell, five CTL, and five HTL. The design followed established mRNA vaccine architecture, beginning with a 5′ cap and Kozak sequence to promote translation initiation, followed by a tissue plasminogen activator signal sequence for secretion and an MHC I-targeting domain to route CTL epitopes to the endoplasmic reticulum. Human beta defensin 1 served as an adjuvant at the N-terminus, connected to helper T-lymphocyte epitopes via GPGPG linkers chosen for their flexibility and ability to promote proper epitope presentation. AAY linkers separated CTL epitopes to facilitate proteasomal cleavage and improve MHC class I antigen processing, while EAAAK linkers maintained structural separation between B-cell epitope domains. A 3′ untranslated region and poly-A tail were appended to bolster mRNA stability and translational efficiency. Safety and physicochemical profiling returned encouraging predictions. The antigenicity scores of constructs 1 and 2 were 0.4984 and 0.4980 respectively, which the authors interpret as an ability to produce antibodies. Both constructs were predicted to be non-allergenic and non-toxic. Molecular weights came out at 120160.44 Da and 120306.28 Da, with theoretical pI values of 8.62 and 8.66 indicating a basic nature. In vitro half-life predictions suggested approximately 30 hours in mammalian reticulocytes. Instability indices of 38.589 and 39.22 classified both as stable proteins, while aliphatic indices of 76.97 and 74.82 reflected thermostability. Negative GRAVY scores of -0.418 and -0.466 confirmed hydrophilic character, and solubility predictions returned scores of 0.345 and 0.296, indicating moderate aqueous solubility. Structural modeling employed AlphaFold 3, SWISS-MODEL, and Phyre2 to predict tertiary structures, followed by refinement with GalaxyRefine. Secondary structure analysis using SOPMA showed construct 1 with 43.66 percent alpha-helix, 10.20 percent extended strands, 0.00 percent beta-turn, and 46.14 percent random coils, while construct 2 exhibited 41.45 percent alpha-helix, 10.20 percent extended strands, 0.00 percent beta-turn, and 48.35 percent random coils. Validation through Ramachandran plot analysis revealed that construct 1 had 95.9 percent of residues in the favored region and construct 2 had 95.0 percent, with only 0.6 and 0.7 percent respectively in disallowed regions. ERRAT quality factors of 97.307 for construct 1 and 96.256 for construct 2 supported the structural reliability of both models. Conformational B-cell epitopes were also mapped onto the three-dimensional structures using ElliPro, identifying six discontinuous epitopes per construct with scores ranging from 0.841 to 0.958. To assess innate immune recognition, the team docked both constructs against Toll-like receptors 2 and 4, pattern recognition receptors that trigger type I interferon and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该研究处于计算设计阶段,尚需实验确认。研究强调所有结果均基于计算机模拟预测,需进一步验证。该方法包括使用VaxiJen、NetCTL和AlphaFold 3等工具进行序列筛选、表位预测和结构建模。

news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：该研究于2026年10月28日发表，事件日期为计算设计工作的日期，但未在证据中明确说明。；地点与对象：该研究使用从国家生物技术信息中心蛋白质数据库中检索到的序列进行，这些序列代表了所有可用大洲的全球数据。目标人群包括受人偏肺病毒影响的儿童、老年人和免疫功能低下个体。；事件：一项计算研究设计了两种针对人偏肺病毒(HMPV)糖蛋白的mRNA 疫苗候选物。结果基于免疫信息学预测，尚需实验确认。；影响与风险：该研究报道了疫苗构建物具有良好的预测抗原性、安全性和结构特性。然而，未报告任何确诊病例、死亡或暴露情况。通过BLASTp分析，已降低了自身免疫交叉反应的风险，并预测这些构建物不会引起过敏或毒性反应。；应对与不确定性：该研究处于计算设计阶段，尚需实验确认。研究强调所有结果均基于计算机模拟预测，需进一步验证。该方法包括使用VaxiJen、NetCTL和AlphaFold 3等工具进行序列筛选、表位预测和结构建模。

The study included 1,499 patients treated in Guangzhou, China, from July 2023 through January 2024. Participants had a mean age of 6.39 years, with a standard deviation of 3.49 years, and 50.7% were male. Most were hospitalized: 1,020 of 1,499 patients, or 68%. Among the hospitalized group, 630 patients, or 62%, had severe infection according to the study’s criteria. Severe disease was particularly associated with the youngest age group, aged 0–5 years. Human parainfluenza virus was the most common pathogen detected alongside M. pneumoniae, occurring in 7.5% of participants, followed by influenza virus in 7.2%. The temporal distributions of these co-infections differed. M. pneumoniae–human parainfluenza virus co-infection predominated from early July to late September 2023 and subsequently decreased, whereas M. pneumoniae–influenza virus co-infection remained common throughout the seven-month study period. These descriptive patterns show that the respiratory pathogens recorded alongside M. pneumoniae varied over time in the Guangzhou cohort. The retrospective observations do not establish the reasons for those changes. Discover more Biology textbook sales Learn Engineering Track Biotech Blood and/or respiratory specimens were collected for respiratory pathogen testing. Patients entered the multivariable analyses if they had completed testing for all eight viral and five bacterial pathogens assessed in the study. The researchers used multivariable logistic regression to examine co-infection patterns in relation to severe clinical outcomes and negative binomial regression to assess hospital stay and fever duration. Hospitalized patients had higher overall rates of both viral and bacterial co-infection with M. pneumoniae than outpatients. The analysis was conducted at one center, and the retrospective design limits how broadly the findings can be generalized beyond the population and clinical setting studied in Guangzhou. Discover more Study Biology infections Infectious Diseases Check Symptoms After adjustment in the multivariable analyses, co-infection with adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, human parainfluenza virus, human rhinovirus, influenza A virus, influenza B virus, Klebsiella pneumoniae or Streptococcus pneumoniae was associated with a significantly higher risk of a severe clinical outcome, longer hospitalization and longer fever duration. These findings describe statistical associations rather than evidence that the additional pathogens caused the worsening or that detecting them necessarily changes clinical decisions. The authors concluded that age-adapted clinical management strategies for M. pneumoniae infection should be developed, with particular attention to specific co-infection patterns. The results are based on 1,499 pediatric and adolescent cases from a single Guangzhou center over a defined seven-month period, and the study did not directly test the effects of any management strategy. analysis.location_and_population: The study was based on 1,499 pediatric and adolescent patients in Guangzhou, China, with a mean age of 6.39 years and 50.7% male.
analysis.event: A single-center retrospective cohort study found that co-infections with various viruses and bacteria, including human parainfluenza virus and influenza virus, were associated with more severe clinical outcomes, longer hospital stays, and longer fever durations in patients with Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 68% of the 1,499 patients were hospitalized, and 62% of hospitalized patients had severe infection. Co-infections with human parainfluenza virus and influenza virus were detected in 7.5% and 7.2% of participants, respectively. Severe disease was particularly associated with the youngest age group (0–5 years).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study did not establish causality for the observed associations. It was a retrospective design, limiting generalizability. The findings describe statistical associations rather than direct causal relationships.

analysis.brief_en: A study conducted in Guangzhou, China, from July 2023 to January 2024 found that co-infections with viruses and bacteria, such as human parainfluenza virus and influenza virus, were linked to more severe clinical outcomes in children and adolescents with Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection. The research, published on October 26, 2026, analyzed 1,499 patients, with a mean age of 6.39 years and 50.7% male. Of these, 68% were hospitalized, and 62% of hospitalized patients had severe infections. The study noted that severe disease was more common in the youngest age group (0–5 years). Co-infections with human parainfluenza virus and influenza virus were detected in 7.5% and 7.2% of participants, respectively. However, the study did not establish causality, and its retrospective design limits the generalizability of the findings. The authors emphasized the need for age-adapted clinical management strategies for Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection, particularly in cases of specific co-infection patterns.
analysis.summary_en: A study conducted in Guangzhou, China, from July 2023 to January 2024 found that co-infections with viruses and bacteria, such as human parainfluenza virus and influenza virus, were linked to more severe clinical outcomes in children and adolescents with Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection. The research, published on October 26, 2026, analyzed 1,499 patients, with a mean age of 6.39 years and 50.7% male. Of these, 68% were hospitalized, and 62% of hospitalized patients had severe infections. The study noted that severe disease was more common in the youngest age group (0–5 years). Co-infections with human parainfluenza virus and influenza virus were detected in 7.5% and 7.2% of participants, respectively. However, the study did not establish causality, and its retrospective design limits the generalizability of the findings. The authors emphasized the need for age-adapted clinical management strategies for Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection, particularly in cases of specific co-infection patterns.

news.content_zh: 一项于2023年7月至2024年1月在中国广州进行的研究发现,肺炎支原体感染的儿童和青少年中,与病毒和细菌(如人副流感病毒和流感病毒)的共感染与更严重的临床结果相关。该研究于2026年10月26日发表,分析了1,499名患者,平均年龄为6.39岁,其中50.7%为男性。这些患者中有68%住院治疗,住院患者中有62%患有严重感染。研究指出,严重疾病在年龄最小的群体(0–5岁)中更为常见。人副流感病毒和流感病毒的共感染分别在7.5%和7.2%的参与者中被检测到。然而,该研究并未建立因果关系,其回顾性设计限制了研究结果的普遍适用性。作者强调,需要针对肺炎支原体感染制定年龄适应性的临床管理策略,特别是在特定共感染模式的情况下。
